What to know
 Greta Cross USA TODAY Nov. 2, 2026 Updated Nov. 3, 2026, 6:23 a.m. ET Hear this story Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3, the final midterm election of President  Donald Trump 's second term, and it will determine who controls Congress.
 With the stakes so high, voters are showing up. More than 54 million Americans have cast early voting ballots, 8 million more than the 2022 midterm election, according to the University of Florida Election Lab . About 45.9 million people cast early votes ahead of 2022 Election Day.
 Each state, not the federal government, determines how Election Day is observed. Some states observe Election Day as a public holiday, some require employers to provide paid time off for voting and others (most states) don't observe the day or require any PTO for employee voting.
 Here's what to know ahead of Election Day, including the states that recognize it as a public holiday.
 America 250, student art, more: See 'I voted' sticker designs for 2026 Is Election Day a federal holiday?
 No, Election Day is not a federal holiday.
 Are banks, post offices and businesses closed on Election Day?
 No, U.S. banks, financial markets, major grocery store chains and retailers are open on Election Day because it is not a federal holiday.
 Which states recognize Election Day as a state holiday?
 Several states recognize Election Day as a public holiday, with some requiring employers to provide paid time off for voting. Here's a look at those states, according to nonprofit Movement Advancement Project :
 States where Election Day is a public holiday, and employers are required to provide PTO for voting
 Illinois
 Hawaii
 Maryland
 New York
 West Virginia
 States where Election Day is a public holiday, and employers are not required to provide PTO for voting
 Delaware
 Indiana
 Kentucky
 Louisana
 Michigan
 Montana
 New Jersey
 Rhode Island
 Virginia

 How many federal holidays are left in 2026?
 According to the  U.S. Office of Personnel Management , there are three federal holidays left in 2026:
 Veterans Day : Wednesday, Nov. 11
 Thanksgiving Day:  Thursday, Nov. 26
 Christmas Day:  Friday, Dec. 25
